title: A flat unramified morphism has unique infinitesimal lifts (is formally etale, hence formally smooth)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] (locally of finite type with open immersion diagonal). Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes over $S$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with closed immersion $i:T\to T'$, structure morphism $T'\to S$, and $T$ regarded as a scheme over $S$ through $T\xrightarrow{i}T'\to S$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $a:T\to X$ be a morphism over $S$. Then there is exactly one morphism $a':T'\to X$ over $S$ with $a'\circ i=a$. In particular $f$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth] (the existence half), and $f$ is formally etale in the sense of Stacks, More on Morphisms, Definition 02HG.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale: 'An unramified flat morphism is formally etale'), with Definition 02HG (definition-formally-etale: exactly one dotted arrow) and Definition 02H0 (definition-formally-smooth: existence of a dotted arrow); [def-weil-unramified-morphism] is Stacks' unramified (Definition 02G4) by Morphisms, Lemma 02GE (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism) (1),(2)

proof.text: *Uniqueness; $f$ is formally unramified.* Since $f$ is unramified, [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified] shows that $f$ is formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]: for a first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine schemes over $S$ and $a:T\to X$ over $S$ there is at most one $a':T'\to X$ over $S$ with $a'\circ i=a$. It remains to prove that such an $a'$ exists. Since $f$ is formally unramified it has a universal first order thickening $X\subset X'$ over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], [lem-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening-exists], with closed immersion $\iota:X\to X'$, ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ ($\mathcal I^2=0$) and structure morphism $h':X'\to S$, $h'\circ\iota=f$, and a conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{X/S}=\iota^*\mathcal I$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified]. The plan (Stacks: 'we have to show that $\mathcal C_{X/S}$ is zero') is to prove $\mathcal C_{X/S}=0$ (steps 2 to 5) and deduce existence from it (step 6, which is Lemma 04FE, (3) implies (1)).

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *The diagonal and the two projections.* Let $p,q:X\times_SX\to X$ be the first and the second projection of the fibre product of $f$ with itself [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\Delta=(\mathrm{id}_X,\mathrm{id}_X):X\to X\times_SX$ the diagonal, so $p\circ\Delta=q\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$. Since $f$ is unramified, $\Delta$ is an open immersion by the definition [def-weil-unramified-morphism] (Stacks quotes Morphisms, Lemma 02GE here, which with the definition of the DAG is part of the definition) [def-weil-open-immersion]; let $D=\Delta(X)\subset X\times_SX$ be the open subscheme it defines and $\delta:X\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ the induced isomorphism, so $\Delta=j\circ\delta$ with $j:D\to X\times_SX$ the inclusion. The morphism $q$ is the base change of $f$ along $f$ (the projection of $X\times_SX$ to the second factor), so $q$ is formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-base-change] applied to the formally unramified $f$ of step 1. The morphism $p$ is the base change of the flat morphism $f$ along $f$ (projection to the first factor), so $p$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *$p^*\mathcal C_{X/S}\cong\mathcal C_q$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-flat-base-change] to the fibre product square with $Y=S$, $W=X$ (the first factor) with the formally unramified morphism $h'=f:W\to S$, and the flat morphism $g=f:X\to S$ (the second factor): then $Z=X\times_SX$, the projection $Z\to X$ to the second factor is $h=q$, and the projection to $W$ is $p$. The lemma gives that $q$ is formally unramified (also seen in step 2) and that the canonical map $p^*\mathcal C_{X/S}\to\mathcal C_q$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X\times_SX}$-modules, where $\mathcal C_q=\mathcal C_{X\times_SX/X}$ is the conormal sheaf of the formally unramified morphism $q$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified], [def-pc-module-pullback]. (Stacks cites Lemma 04F9 together with the flatness of $p$, which is the flatness of $g$ in the lemma.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *$\mathcal C_q|_D=0$.* The open subscheme $D=\Delta(X)$ maps isomorphically to $X$ under $q$: $q|_D\circ\delta=q\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\delta$ is an isomorphism, so $e:=q|_D:D\to X$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\delta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-restriction] applied to $q$ with $V=D$ and $U=X$, $e$ is formally unramified and $\mathcal C_q|_D\cong\mathcal C_{D/X}$. Now $D\subset D$ (identity closed immersion, ideal sheaf $0$) with structure morphism $e$ is a universal first order thickening of $D$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]: given a first order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $X$ with $i_T:T\to T'$, $b:T'\to X$, and $a:T\to D$ with $e\circ a=b\circ i_T$, the morphism $a'=e^{-1}\circ b$ satisfies $e\circ a'=b$ and $a'\circ i_T=e^{-1}\circ e\circ a=a$, and it is the only one since $e\circ a'=b$ forces $a'=e^{-1}\circ b$. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening-exists] every universal first order thickening of $D$ over $X$ is isomorphic to this one compatibly with $D$, so the ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] of $D$ in it is $0$ and $\mathcal C_{D/X}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified]. Hence $\mathcal C_q|_D=0$ ('$\mathcal C_q|_{\Delta(X)}=\mathcal C_{X/X}=0$' in Stacks, by Lemma 04FA).

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *$\mathcal C_{X/S}=0$.* Pullback of modules satisfies $\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $(v\circ u)^*\cong u^*v^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Since $p\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\Delta=j\circ\delta$, steps 3 and 4 give $\mathcal C_{X/S}\cong\Delta^*p^*\mathcal C_{X/S}\cong\Delta^*\mathcal C_q\cong\delta^*j^*\mathcal C_q\cong\delta^*(\mathcal C_q|_D)=\delta^*0=0$, where $j^*\mathcal C_q\cong\mathcal C_q|_D$ because $j$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]. ('In other words, the pullback of $\mathcal C_{X/S}$ to $X$ via the identity morphism is zero, i.e., $\mathcal C_{X/S}=0$.')

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *Existence of the lift (Lemma 04FE, (3) implies (1)).* Let $X\subset X'$, $\iota$, $\mathcal I$, $h'$ be as in step 1. As $X'$ is a first order thickening of $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $\iota$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces and $\iota^\sharp:\mathcal O_{X'}\to\iota_*\mathcal O_X$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; hence $\mathcal O_X=\iota^{-1}\mathcal O_{X'}/\iota^{-1}\mathcal I$ and $\iota^*\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\iota^{-1}\mathcal O_{X'}}\iota^{-1}\mathcal I=\iota^{-1}\mathcal I/(\iota^{-1}\mathcal I)^2=\iota^{-1}\mathcal I$ as $\mathcal I^2=0$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. By step 5, $\iota^{-1}\mathcal I=\mathcal C_{X/S}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified], so $\mathcal I=0$ ($\iota$ is a homeomorphism), $\iota^\sharp$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings, and $\iota$ is an isomorphism of schemes ('the universal first order thickening of $X$ over $S$ is equal to $X$'). Now let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes over $S$, with $i:T\to T'$, $b:T'\to S$, and $a:T\to X$ with $f\circ a=b\circ i$. By the universal property of $X'$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] there is $a'':T'\to X'$ with $h'\circ a''=b$ and $a''\circ i=\iota\circ a$. Put $a'=\iota^{-1}\circ a''$; then $f\circ a'=h'\circ\iota\circ\iota^{-1}\circ a''=b$ and $a'\circ i=\iota^{-1}\circ\iota\circ a=a$. With step 1, $a'$ is the only morphism $T'\to X$ over $S$ with $a'\circ i=a$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FE (lemma-characterize-formally-etale), (3) implies (1) via (2), as used in the proof of Lemma 04FF

proof.text: *Consequences.* By steps 1 and 6, for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine schemes over $S$ and every $a:T\to X$ over $S$ there is exactly one $a':T'\to X$ over $S$ with $a'\circ i=a$; this is the definition of formally etale (Stacks Definition 02HG). The existence half is the definition of formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth], so $f$ is formally smooth.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 04FF/02HG/02H0 and kept (stmt_deps unchanged). Mathlib has no lifting statement without finite presentation (Etale.of_formallyUnramified_of_flat needs LocallyOfFinitePresentation), so no leaf. Proof written in 7 steps following the proof of 04FF exactly: f is formally unramified (02HE) giving uniqueness; p flat (01U9), q formally unramified (02HB); p^*C_{X/S} = C_q (04F9); C_q|_{Delta(X)} = C_{X/X} = 0 (04FA); hence C_{X/S}=0; then existence through the universal first order thickening (04FE (3)=>(1), written out as a step). New nodes: definitions of formally unramified morphisms (02H8, Mathlib leaf via FormallyUnramified.hom_ext/of_hom_ext), universal first order thickening (04F2/04F4(1)) and conormal sheaf (04F4(2)); lemmas 02HE and 02HB (Mathlib leaves), 01U9 (Mathlib leaf), 04F3 (existence and uniqueness of universal thickenings), 04F8+04F9 (flat base change), 04FA (open restriction), the last three unsplit.
